subject: Meteorology
title: The Enhanced Fujita Scale
description: A 60-second lesson on The Enhanced Fujita Scale.

hook.text: Tornadoes are rated after the fact—by surveying the damage they leave behind, not by measuring wind directly.

buildup.text: The Enhanced Fujita (EF) scale ranges from EF0 (light damage) to EF5 (incredible destruction).

discovery.text: EF5 tornadoes have estimated winds over 320 km/h—strong enough to sweep away well-built homes entirely.

twist.text: We rarely measure tornado wind speeds directly—most ratings are educated estimates based on damage indicators.

climax.text: Only about 1% of tornadoes reach EF4 or EF5—but they cause the vast majority of tornado deaths.

punchline.text: The rating comes after the storm—based on what's left standing.

quiz.question: How are tornadoes rated on the Enhanced Fujita scale?
